pages.text: "It will not come undone! Not at all!" Nils the little bear tugged his sled rope. The more he pulled, the tighter the knot became. The sled sat all alone in the snow on the hill.
"Today I will zoom all the way down that hill." Nils pointed downhill with his nose. But the rope was still a hard lump.
Angry, Nils kicked the sled. Thump! It flipped over, scattering snow. "You silly sled!" Nils shouted.
Birds perched on branches fluttered away. Nils sat in the snow and stamped his feet. His chest felt hot, and his throat tight.
Grandpa Bruno from the forest cabin walked up the snowy hill. He knelt beside Nils. "Nils, you are full of hot feelings. You need somewhere to let them out."
Grandpa rounded his mouth and breathed out slowly. A stream of white breath drifted into the snowy sky. "Let the heat out like this. Breathe out—a white cloud!"
Nils puffed out his tummy, then breathed out too. One little white cloud, then another, drifted over the snow. "Breathe out—a white cloud! My throat is not tight anymore." His shoulders relaxed.
Grandpa held one side of the knot with his broad palm. This time, Nils pulled gently, little by little. Slip—the rope came loose and stretched out.

"It is untied!" Nils raised both paws above his head. "One, take a big breath and blow out! Two, let your shoulders drop! Three, try again gently!" He looped the rope over his paw and sat on the sled.
Nils zoomed downhill. Grandpa caught him in both paws. Even when angry, a big breath out helps you try again. "I will go for another ride! Breathe out—a white cloud!"
